rows: The Weighhouse. Where every scale in the ward gets its number checked against the customs man's own.
Berth ledger, tariff scales, the impound yard out back. Nothing crosses that quay without going through there first.
Ask Crell. He has read every manifest that ever came off a boat, and he remembers most of them.
Good scales, honest weights, and a harbormaster who has caught me shorting a customer exactly once. Once was enough.
The tariff schedule is posted on the wall and nobody has ever liked reading it.
The Weighhouse keeps the district's books straight. Cross Crell and you have crossed the whole customs house.
I have stood outside that door more mornings than I can count. The queue never gets shorter.
The Gilded Gull. Captains' tavern, up on the Tarwalk. Charts on the walls and the good wine, if you can pay for it.
Factors do their deals there over a table nobody else is allowed to sit at.
Ask around the Gull if you want to know what came in on the last tide. Somebody there always does.
Best charts on the waterfront hang on that wall, and half of them are wrong on purpose.
I have slept better nights on a rolling deck than on a bench in that taproom, but the wine is worth the trip.
Not a house for the likes of me. Captains and factors drink there, and they do not buy for strangers.
I have stood outside the Gull's window more than once, just for the smell of it.
The Mission of the Flame. Soup, a bunk if you need one, and a disciple awake at every hour to give it.
Father Maell keeps it. White garb, and not everyone out here trusts the sight of it, but the bowls are full.
The Mission never closes its door, whatever the hour. That is the whole of what the Flame asks of it.
Father Maell has fed this ward through worse winters than this one. I would not bet against him feeding it through the next.
They will feed you at the Mission and not ask what you did to get hungry. I have never worked out the trick of it.
The Drowned Hold. Condemned warehouse, east end. Been empty nine years, officially.
Half its floor is sagging toward the water and nobody has fixed it. Nobody official goes near it either.
Lamplight under the door some nights, they say. I have not gone to look.
I do not go near the Drowned Hold after dark, and neither should you. Empty buildings do not light their own lamps.
Condemned nine years and never pulled down. That is a question somebody higher up has never answered for me either.
We do not patrol the Drowned Hold. There is nothing there to protect, officially.
The Watch-Post, up at the top of the Rise. Notice board out front, and a gibbet cage that has not always been empty.
That is where you go if you want the Watch to actually listen.
My post. Notice board, holding cell, and a view down the whole Rise to the water. I have had worse.
Come up and see it sometime. Best view of the harbour in the ward, and I will even pour you what passes for tea up there.
The ground penny. Quarterly rent on the earth under your house, owed to whoever holds the charge on the plot.
Nobody in this ward owns the ground they stand on. Not even the man who collects for it.
Pay the ground penny on time and a Den Duke never has cause to look at you twice. That is the whole trick of it.
I have seen a man lease himself to work off a bad quarter's penny. It happens more than the Duke likes admitted.
The Flame. An office, a vigil, kept at the Mission. Ask there if you want more than that from me.
The Divine Light holds this ward together more than the Watch does, if you ask me, which nobody official ever does.
The Flame is not mine to hand you. It is an office and a vigil, and I only keep the second of those.
Six powers, and the Flame is the greatest of them. Ask any Runemaster and they will tell you the same.
A passport. Papers for the Inner Wall gate. Even a Wielder presents one, they say, so do not think your face buys you past it.
No passport, no gate. I have turned back better-dressed men than you for forgetting theirs.
A scalp. Vermin bounty, paid at the counter, signed for by the Flame before the knife and not after.
A scalp is honest coin if the rats are honest vermin. Mind whose mark you are carrying when you bring one in.
Scalps are the one bounty we do not ask questions about, so long as the Flame's mark is on the sack.
The tide. Two levels, high and low, and the Outfall grate only opens at the low one. Everything under the quay minds it.
Watch the tide before you watch anything else out here. It has drowned better sailors than the harbour ever did on purpose.
